messages:
maya: Quick sync idea 1: Make gateway retries telemetry-aware so we don't double-retry and so billing/latency attribution is sane.

sam: Sounds useful. What's the failure mode today?

maya: Right now edge and upstream each apply retry logic. If gateway thinks an upstream attempt failed (e.g., timeout) it retries, even though upstream actually completed the work. That inflates attempt counts and confuses SLOs. Streaming makes it worse: partial chunks might be emitted then retried, producing duplicates.

liam: Example?

maya: client -> gateway (hedge) -> upstream replica A. A finishes but its final ack is delayed. Gateway times out and forwards to replica B. B also finishes. Billing and token accounting show 2 attempts. Dashboards show increased 95p latency and retry spikes.

rachel: That also breaks our QA tracing since we can't tell which attempt generated the final tokens.

ops-bot: [metric] gateway.retry_attempts spiked 2x at 03/09 14:12 UTC

sam: Proposal: gateway should attach minimal opaque fields to every forwarded request so we can correlate attempts across layers and let upstream declare a verdict. Candidates:
```
# gateway -> upstream
x-rw-attempt-id: <uuid>
x-rw-parent-id: <uuid?>   # when hedging/spawning
x-rw-idempotency-key: <client-provided?>
x-rw-retry-scope: conservative|optimistic

# upstream -> gateway
x-rw-upstream-verdict: retryable|terminal|served-locally
x-rw-upstream-reason: timeout|oom|model-error|partial
x-rw-chargeable: true|false
```

liam: How does this interact with streaming? If a retry happens mid-stream, we can't rewind tokens.

maya: Two phased approach:
- short term (beta): conservative: if a stream is midflight and gateway hasn't seen a final terminal header, mark upstream as 'uncertain' and avoid gateway-initiated midstream retry. Fall back to soft hedges (route subsequent requests to alternate replicas).
- long term: implement resumable fragments: upstream supports `x-rw-fragment-offset` and `x-rw-resume-token` so gateway can resume without re-emitting prior tokens. Requires KV checkpointing in model proxy.

rachel: For rollout, make telemetry-aware retries opt-in per route. Start at 1% traffic then ramp.

sam: Telemetry integration: emit metrics with attempt_id label: gateway.attempt.latency{attempt_id=...} and gateway.attempt.outcome. Also annotate traces: keep one trace id but add attempt_id as span attribute so we can see which attempt produced final response.

liam: Edge-case: clients with their own retry logic. We should rely on idempotency-key or generate our own and dedupe duplicate attempts arriving within window T. If idempotency-key present, gateway should collapse duplicates to one live attempt and respond with an idempotency conflict when appropriate.

maya: Also propose chargeability flag: upstream can set `x-rw-chargeable: false` when it detects the request was replayed and shouldn't be billed again. Gateway reconciles billing using attempt_id map and upstream chargeable hints.

sam: Security: these headers are sensitive. Strip any external attempt headers and gateway must authoritatively sign `x-rw-attempt-id` or HMAC it to prevent spoofing.

devx-bot: Note: SDKs should expose a simple idempotency helper and document the retry semantics for customers.

rachel: Migration plan:
- phase 0: RFC + spec for header taxonomy and mapping table
- phase 1: gateway implementation to emit attempt headers + conservative streaming behavior; expose per-route config retry.telemetry=false|true
- phase 2: upstream adapters honor verdict headers and emit chargeable flag; trace/metrics plumbing
- phase 3: resumable streaming and KV checkpoints for advanced routes

maya: Quick engineering checklist:
- gateway: header gen, strip inbound spoofing, metrics labels, tracing annotations
- model-proxy: accept headers, emit verdict header, optionally support fragment offsets
- billing: aggregator reconciler to mark non-chargeable duplicates
- devx: SDK helper + docs

sam: Any objections to conservative streaming default?

liam: No objections. Prefer conservative until we validate KV-resume robustness.

rachel: +1. Also add alerting: if we see >0.5% of traffic with `x-rw-upstream-reason=partial` escalate.

maya: Cool. I'll write RFC with header spec, security note about HMAC signing, and a diagram showing attempt lifecycle. Will include a route config snippet for canary.

sam: Thanks. Let's link the RFC in this thread when ready.

maya: Thanks all :white_check_mark:
